prompt:
Write 10 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a low-speed head-on collision claim, in time order. Injury: shoulder injury. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1201; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- Years ago the patient had a small strain in the same area that healed fully.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- A few old scratches may be older than this crash.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim received for a low-speed head-on collision. The insured's policy is active and the driver is named on it. Claimant is represented by counsel, so all further contact will go through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: Reviewed the police report and statements from two witnesses. Both confirm the vehicle was involved in the collision and that the claimant was seated in the vehicle at the time.

Entry 3: Photos from the scene and the other driver's account match the described impact. Vehicle damage is mostly consistent with the reported force of the crash, though a few older scratches may predate this loss and will be noted separately.

Entry 4: Nothing in the file suggests the damage occurred before the coverage start date. Prior policy records were checked and show no earlier loss on this vehicle.

Entry 5: Claimant reported a shoulder injury following the collision. The injury is plausible for an impact of this type and direction.

Entry 6: Medical records show the claimant had a minor strain in the same area several years ago, which healed fully. This history has been noted and does not appear to be related to the current complaint.

Entry 7: Counsel forwarded the initial treatment records. Care followed a typical course, with physical therapy and follow-up visits tapering as the claimant's range of motion improved.

Entry 8: Spoke with the claimant's attorney, who confirmed the client's account. In each conversation to date, the claimant has described the collision the same way.

Entry 9: Reviewed the latest treatment notes. The provider reports steady improvement and fewer visits scheduled going forward, which is consistent with the expected recovery timeline.

Entry 10: File is current. Remaining items are the final medical bill and the vehicle repair invoice. Reserve will be reviewed once both are received.
